data.body:
Closing evidence. The fix merged as `e3d8b853afde` ("Bound the Jira DC harness store
copy"), Gerrit change 3012, `Verified +1` and `LLM-Review +1`.

AC1 — peak disk no longer tracks total store size. The copy is a bounded, deterministic
slice: all store metadata, all bridge-named directories, and canonical-id tickets sampled
at an even stride. Cost is now a function of the sample bound, not of how many tickets the
store has accumulated.

AC2 — the snapshot is no longer buffered whole in RAM. `git archive` streams into `tar`
rather than being captured as `.stdout`.

AC3 — each fixture reclaims its tree at teardown, so the three modules stop summing their
peaks.

AC4 — still a REAL scrubbed store. The slice is drawn from the live tickets branch;
synthetic tickets would have relocated the coverage gap instead of closing it. The
even-stride sampling is deliberate so the slice spans the store's whole history rather
than one contiguous era.

AC5 — live-lane evidence. `external-integration.yml` run `35537795041`, job
`jira-dc-harness`, on `main` at `873340add`: **success in 22m27s**. Zero occurrences of
all 5 disk-exhaustion strings, including `You are running out of disk space` and
`Out of diskspace`. Collection was `collected=75 executed=74 skipped=1`, finishing
`74 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfailed in 743.91s` — so the fail-on-all-skip guard did not trip
and the lane genuinely exercised the harness rather than skipping past it.

The earlier run `35534905486` at `ba8782727` predates the fix and stands only as a
before-data-point.

AC6 — no CI provider is required. The disk-cost guarantee is driven by repo-tier tests
against real temporary repositories, so it is checked on every commit and behaves
identically locally. Nothing in the changed code is GitHub Actions specific.
